Dr. Rima E. Laibow is a controversial figure known for her promotion of alternative medicine and various conspiracy theories. Trained as a psychiatrist, Laibow has frequently spoken against vaccines and has propagated theories about health-related government conspiracies. She has been an outspoken critic of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and other health regulatory agencies, alleging that they work in tandem with pharmaceutical companies to the detriment of public health.

One of her most notable controversies involves her advocacy against vaccinations, where she posits that vaccines are part of a larger agenda to control the population's health. This stance has placed her at odds with the mainstream medical community and public health institutions, which emphasize the importance of vaccination in preventing diseases.

Dr. Laibow's theories have occasionally intersected with the ideas promoted by Alex Jones, a known conspiracy theorist and media personality. She has appeared on his platform, Infowars, to discuss topics like the alleged dangers of vaccines and governmental overreach in health matters. This affiliation has further polarized public opinion about her work, gaining her both fervent supporters and vocal detractors.

While some view her as a champion of personal health freedom, others criticize her for spreading misinformation that could potentially harm public health efforts. Dr. Laibow continues to be an active figure in the alternative health community, often participating in conferences and online discussions centered around her controversial viewpoints.

== Personal Life ==
Dr. Rima E. Laibow was married to [[General Albert Stubblebine]]
